questions.enonce_markdown:
Clearly bring out John's approach to the person of Christ and his mission.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Fourth Gospel presents Jesus in a way distinct from the Synoptics. John writes from the conviction that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God (20:31), and organises his Gospel around this belief. His approach to the person and mission of Christ is theological: it asks who Jesus is and why he was sent.

**1. The person of Christ.**
- *The Word.* The prologue says that "in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (1:1), and "the Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (1:14). Jesus is pre-existent, divine, and fully human.
- *Son of God.* He is the unique Son who is in the closest relation to the Father (1:18; 5:19-23; 10:30; 14:9).
- *The "I am" sayings.* He uses the divine phrase "I am" with images: the bread of life (6:35), the light of the world (8:12), the door (10:7), the good shepherd (10:11), the resurrection and the life (11:25), the way, the truth and the life (14:6), the true vine (15:1), and the absolute "I am" (8:58).
- *Real humanity.* He is tired and thirsty (4:6-7), weeps (11:35), is troubled (12:27), and dies (19:30). The Gospel avoids denying his flesh.
- *Other titles.* Lamb of God, Messiah, King of Israel, Son of Man, Saviour of the world (4:42), Lord and God (20:28).

**2. The mission of Christ.**
- *Sent by the Father.* Jesus repeatedly says that he was sent and does the will of the Father (4:34; 5:30; 6:38).
- *To reveal the Father.* "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father" (14:9).
- *To give life.* "I came that they may have life and have it abundantly" (10:10); the signs show this, and John 3:16 says that God gave the Son so that those who believe may not perish but have eternal life.
- *To bring light and judgment.* His coming forces a decision (3:19; 9:39).
- *To die and be glorified.* His "hour" is the cross and resurrection, where he is "lifted up" (3:14; 12:32). He lays down his life for his sheep (10:11, 17-18).
- *To gather and unite.* He draws all people to himself (12:32), forms a community, gives a new commandment to love one another (13:34), prays for unity (17), and promises the Spirit, the Paraclete (14-16).
- *To send.* "As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you" (20:21).

**3. Method.** John uses signs, long discourses, dialogues (Nicodemus, the Samaritan woman) and a symbolic language to lead the reader to faith. He is selective (20:30-31).

**Conclusion.** John's approach is a high Christology: Jesus is the divine Word made flesh who reveals the Father and gives eternal life through his death and resurrection. His mission is to bring humanity into life and communion with God, and to continue through the community of believers.
